title: Intervention-oriented views: recurring locations, pedestrian corridors and audit candidates

rules.recurrence: Reports (of 9, 2016 to 2024) that list the place name: 7 or more = persistent, 5 to 6 = frequent, 3 to 4 = repeated, 1 to 2 = occasional.
rules.nameMatching: Names are matched after removing case, spaces and punctuation. Twelve reviewed spelling pairs are merged (listed in aliasesMerged); similar names that fail the test are listed in notMerged.
rules.evidenceTier: Tier 1: pedestrian crash-prone in 2024 and listed in 5 or more reports. Tier 2: listed in 5 or more reports, or pedestrian crash-prone and listed in 3 or more. Tier 3: pedestrian crash-prone or listed in 3 or more. Tier 4: otherwise. A tier says how strong the crash evidence is, not how dangerous a place is.
rules.pedestrianCorridor: A road with two or more 2024 pedestrian crash-prone zones, by the road name printed beside each zone.
rules.sparselyMapped: No mapped crossing and no mapped signal within 250 m, and under 0.2 km of mapped footway within 250 m. It describes the map, not the street: 80 of 93 zones have no mapped crossing within 250 m, so absence on the map is not used to rank.

notMerged: plausibly the same locality, not confirmed
caveats: Zone positions are hand-placed with an estimated accuracy of 150 m to 5 km; an audit area is an area, not a point.
The Traffic Police re-draw the zone list every year and apply a count threshold, so a place leaving the list is not a place becoming safe, and a place joining it is not proof of a new hazard.
Crash counts are within each zone, not all crashes on a road or in a ward. The 2022 list prints no road: roads there are those a later report assigns to the same name.
Mapped infrastructure comes from OpenStreetMap and is a lower bound.
Nothing here establishes cause, responsibility or what should be built. Field verification is needed first.
